messages:
maria: Customer Cypress (dedicated) reporting ~3x p99 since ~03:00UTC, started after midnight deploy. They see long tail on generation step, not enqueue. Ticket: CS-4821 :grimacing:
samir: Can you paste the p99/time breakdown from console? routing/model id/host? :eyes:
maria: pasted snippet from console logs:
```
model: redwood-v2-13b-q4
route: cypress-prod
p50: 54ms
p95: 120ms
p99: 980ms (median token time jump)
hosts: gpu-pool-5a (95% of traffic)
errors: 0
```
oliver: Looks like KV cache misses maybe? Did the model variant change (quantization/kv-layout) in the deploy?
maria: deploy-bot: anonymous deploy 2026-03-17T00:45Z by @deploy_pipeline (redwood-v2-13b-q4) - config: batch_max_tokens=1024, kv_shard=auto
jess: I pushed a small rollout for this customer yesterday (canary to 10%). Maybe rollout expanded earlier than planned. @deploy-bot can you confirm active percent on route cypress-prod?
deploy-bot: active_percent(cypress-prod, redwood-v2-13b-q4) = 100%
samir: Ok that explains timing. If kv_shard/quant change caused miss pattern, tail can spike. Can we force route to previous variant (redwood-v2-13b-q4-legacy) for cypress-prod as emergency fallback?
maria: support-bot: CS-4821 update: customer is sensitive, wants ETA. They can tolerate brief failover.
oliver: Before failover, can we capture a 60s profile from one of the hosts showing kernel times and kv hit rate? Command: `ssh gpu-pool-5a && /opt/redwood/bin/profile --duration 60 --out /tmp/profile.pb`
samir: I can run that, will grab traces and kv metrics. scheduling now.
samir: (later) profile uploaded to /s3/redwood/profiles/2060123456-cypress-60s.pb, kv_hit_rate: 0.62, avg kv_latency: 3.8ms, cpu kernel time rising at tail
jess: If kv_hit_rate is 62% that's lower than expected for production with persistent cache. Could be that cache was flushed during deploy. Any cache-flush events?
maria: I see a cache TTL bump in the deploy notes -> kv_cache_ttl reset to 0 during migration step. That aligns.
oliver: Proposed plan: 1) revert cypress-prod to previous variant (manual route change), 2) restart cache warmers on affected hosts, 3) run smoke and monitor p99 for 15m. Who can own 1 and 2?
samir: I'll do 1 (route revert) and 2 (kick warmers). I'll coordinate with infra to avoid double restarts.
maria: after revert, please post `console metrics p99 cypress-prod 15m` and tag me.
samir: done: route set -> redwood-v2-13b-q4-legacy, warmers restarted on gpu-pool-5a, running smoke.
samir: (5m) p99 dropped to 140ms, p95 110ms. Looks back to normal range. :tada:
maria: great, will update customer and close CS-4821 if stable for 30m. Thanks all.
jess: follow-ups: add a deploy guard to prevent kv_ttl reset on live routes, add a preflight that checks cache-hit delta on canary expand. I'm filing an RFC.
maria: assigned RFC -> eng-runtime/rfcs/avoid-kv-ttl-reset.cc: @oliver @jess
oliver: +1, will review.
sre-bot: autoscaler logged burst on gpu-pool-5a at 03:12 UTC, scaled +2 nodes; no OOMs.
maria: leaving this thread open until 30m stable window, thanks. :white_check_mark:
